name: Navbar
description: Sticky site header on translucent glass: brand at the start, links and actions at the end, content centred at page width.
whenToUse: The top bar of a website or app shell: logo, a few top-level links, one call to action.
whenNotToUse: Switching views inside a page — use Tabs.
Long lists of links — keep two to five, and move the rest into a DropdownMenu or the footer.

classes.ayy-navbar: Root, usually a <header>. Sticky, 72px tall (--ayy-size-header), glass background with a hairline under it. Anchor jumps land below it.
classes.ayy-navbar__inner: Centred row at page width (--ayy-size-container) with the page gutter.
classes.ayy-navbar__brand: Logo / name link at the start.
classes.ayy-navbar__nav: <nav> of links. It and everything after it sit at the end. Scrolls sideways if the links don't fit.
classes.ayy-navbar__link: Top-level link. aria-current="page" marks the page you're on.
classes.ayy-navbar__actions: Group of buttons (theme toggle, call to action). Next to the brand, or at the end after the nav.

js: navbarClass, navbarInnerClass, navbarBrandClass, navbarNavClass, navbarLinkClass, navbarActionsClass constants.

react.import: import { Navbar, NavbarBrand, NavbarNav, NavbarLink, NavbarActions } from "ayywi/react";

a11y: Use <header> for the bar and <nav aria-label="Main"> for the links; one main nav per page.
Mark the current page with aria-current="page", not only with colour.
Put a .ayy-skip-link before the navbar so keyboard users can jump past it.
do: Keep one call to action in the actions group (a ring or primary button, size sm).
On phones keep the brand, one or two links and the call to action; move the rest into a menu.
dont: Don't give the navbar its own background colour; the glass token keeps both themes right.
Don't nest a second navbar inside the page.
